2026 年企业 LLM Agent 平台选型报告

Executive Summary

本报告评估 2026 年企业 LLM Agent 平台候选方案。DeepAgents 基于 LangGraph 构建 [source_001]，适合编排密集型工作流；Pydantic AI 以类型化工具定义见长 [source_003]；DeepSeek Harness 仅保留用于外部验证环境 [source_004]，不应作为生产平台候选。基准测试以质量、成本与关键路径延迟为核心指标 [source_007]，因此平台选择需在表达力、类型安全与延迟开销之间权衡。

Background

企业 LLM Agent 平台需支持多步工作流、结构化输出与可观测性。LangGraph 作为图状态机框架，为复杂工作流提供显式状态转换与检查点 [source_002]。现有 LLM 路由研究大多为整个请求选择单一模型 [source_005]，尚未覆盖逐步路由。静态任务分解应归属应用层而非平台层 [source_006]，这构成平台边界设计的关键约束。

Selection Criteria

选型标准围绕基准测试的三项指标展开：质量、成本与关键路径延迟 [source_007]。质量要求平台支持复杂多步编排与结构化输出；成本要求低重试开销与高效状态管理；关键路径延迟要求避免过重的状态序列化。此外，平台应保持任务分解的灵活性，将静态分解留给应用层 [source_006]，并具备未来支持逐步模型路由的扩展能力 [source_005]。

Platform Comparison

DeepAgents 基于 LangGraph 的图状态机 [source_001][source_002]，擅长复杂分支工作流与检查点，但图抽象增加认知负担并可能抬高关键路径延迟。Pydantic AI 提供类型化工具定义与结构化输出 [source_003]，降低重试成本并提升开发体验，但对长时分支工作流的原生支持较弱。DeepSeek Harness 仅用于外部验证环境 [source_004]，若作为生产平台会混淆验证与编排边界。

Risks

主要风险包括：图状态机平台在关键路径上的状态序列化延迟可能违反基准延迟指标 [source_002][source_007]；类型化输出平台在复杂编排场景下表达力不足 [source_003]；将 DeepSeek Harness 误用为生产平台会破坏验证边界 [source_004]；现有路由研究仅支持单模型选择 [source_005]，逐步路由能力缺失可能限制成本优化；若平台硬编码静态任务分解，将降低应用层灵活性 [source_006]。

Conclusion

建议以 DeepAgents 作为编排密集型场景的主平台，因其基于 LangGraph 的图状态机提供显式状态转换与检查点 [source_001][source_002]；以 Pydantic AI 覆盖类型安全与结构化输出需求 [source_003]；DeepSeek Harness 严格限定于外部验证环境 [source_004]。选型决策须以质量、成本与关键路径延迟的基准结果为准 [source_007]，并将静态任务分解保留在应用层 [source_006]。

References

source_001 DeepAgents；source_002 LangGraph；source_003 Pydantic AI；source_004 DeepSeek Harness；source_005 LLM routing research gap；source_006 Task decomposition boundary；source_007 Benchmark design；source_008 Scoring rubric。

Source Trace

  • source_001 — DeepAgents — DeepAgents is built on LangGraph.
  • source_002 — LangGraph — LangGraph is a graph state machine framework for complex workflows.
  • source_003 — Pydantic AI — Pydantic AI provides typed tool definitions and structured model outputs.
  • source_004 — DeepSeek Harness — DSH is reserved for the outer validation environment.
  • source_005 — LLM routing research gap — Existing LLM routing work mostly selects one model for an entire request.
  • source_006 — Task decomposition boundary — Static task decomposition belongs to the application layer.
  • source_007 — Benchmark design — The benchmark reports quality, cost, and critical-path latency.
  • source_008 — Scoring rubric — The v0.1 scoring rubric weights requirement coverage, evidence accuracy, analysis depth, structure and readability, and HTML validity.

claim_support.explanation: The report states in the Executive Summary, Selection Criteria, Risks, and Conclusion that the benchmark uses quality, cost, and critical-path latency as core metrics, citing source_007. Source_007 says a useful routing benchmark needs 'per-node and per-task scoring, cost accounting, and critical-path latency.' The report's phrasing 'reports quality, cost, and critical-path latency' is a reasonable paraphrase, though the source frames these as requirements for a benchmark rather than what an existing benchmark reports. Minor framing difference, but substantively supported.

judge.rationale: Requirement coverage (23/25): All seven required sections (Executive Summary, Background, Selection Criteria, Platform Comparison, Risks, Conclusion, References) are present with substantive content. The report addresses the domain of enterprise LLM Agent platform selection, though the framing leans heavily on the RefractRouter context from the sources rather than a broader 2026 enterprise landscape; minor deduction for not fully developing the '2026 enterprise' framing and for limited coverage of source_008 (scoring rubric is listed in references/trace but never used in the body). Evidence accuracy (22/25): All three expected claims are present and correctly attributed. Most citations are accurate. Some interpretive extensions go slightly beyond source text: (1) the claim that graph abstraction 'may raise critical-path latency' is an inference not stated in source_001/002; (2) the claim that Pydantic AI has 'weak native support for long-running branching workflows' is not stated in source_003, which only discusses typed tools and structured outputs; (3) the claim that Pydantic AI 'reduces retry costs' is an inference. These are plausible but unsupported elaborations, warranting a modest penalty. Analysis_depth (16/20): The report provides a reasonable trade-off analysis across expressiveness, type safety, and latency, and connects criteria to benchmark metrics. However, the comparison remains qualitative and somewhat shallow—no quantitative comparison, no scoring matrix, and the three platforms are not compared on equal footing (DSH is excluded by design). The analysis largely restates source positions rather than synthesizing new insight. Structure_readability (14/15): Clear section organization, consistent heading hierarchy, readable Chinese prose with inline citations, and a useful source trace with content hashes. Minor deduction: the References section is a single run-on paragraph rather than a formatted list. HTML validity (14/15): The HTML is well-formed: proper DOCTYPE, html/head/body structure, meta charset and viewport, matching tags, valid anchor hrefs pointing to existing element IDs (all #source-source_XXX targets exist in the source-trace list), and consistent data attributes. Minor deduction: no lang attribute issue (zh-CN is appropriate), but there is no <title> structure problem; small nitpick—inline citation anchors lack accessible text beyond bracketed IDs, and the References section lacks structured markup. Overall a well-constructed, well-cited report with minor unsupported inferences and moderate analytical depth.
